name: Credit spreads
summary: US high-yield spreads 3.48%, widest in a year but inside the 4% Watch line
state: The US high-yield option-adjusted spread was 3.48% on 5 Nov, about 39bp wider than a month earlier and at its widest in a year, but inside the 4% Watch line and the 100bp monthly widening line (FRED). No broad credit squeeze had been reported as of 7 Nov.
for_you: Riskier companies are paying slightly more to borrow; conditions remain within normal ranges. Describes market conditions only; it is not advice.
rubric_hit: HY OAS 3.48% below the 4% Watch line

sources.title: FRED — ICE BofA US High Yield OAS

why: High-yield spreads show how much lenders demand to fund weaker companies — an early warning of defaults and credit crunches.
drivers: Default expectations, risk appetite, rates, private-credit stress, fund outflows.

rubric.alert: HY OAS > 6.0%, or widened > 200bp in a month.
rubric.watch: HY OAS 4.0–6.0%, or widened > 100bp in a month.
